original_question: Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c>0 such that for every n>=4, the maximum size g_{P_3}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which every pairwise intersection contains a path with three edges satisfies g_{P_3}(n) <= (1-c) 2^{C(n,2)-1}.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.5 (Alon, Spencer): the P_3-intersecting problem asking for an absolute-constant-factor improvement over the trivial upper bound g_{P_3}(n) <= 2^{binom(n,2)-1}. This is the exact official formulation your draft is aiming at, not the earlier stronger equality conjecture for P_3 that the paper says was disproved. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the main mathematical content: it uses the correct extremal quantity g_{P_3}(n), the correct pairwise-intersection condition, the correct absolute-constant form of the bound, and the correct range n >= 4. In substance, it is already Conjecture 4.5 once the paper’s definitions of H-intersecting families and g_H(n) are made explicit. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
missing_details: Specify that the objects are simple labelled graphs on the common vertex set [n]. The paper defines g_H(n) via families of graphs on [n]. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

State explicitly that P_3 is the paper’s notation for the path with three edges. This matters because other conventions sometimes use P_4 for that graph. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

Define P_3-intersecting precisely: for every G_1,G_2 in the family, the edge-intersection G_1 ∩ G_2 contains a copy of P_3. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

Define g_{P_3}(n) formally as the maximum size of a P_3-intersecting family of graphs on [n], rather than only describing it informally. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
refined_question: Let P_3 denote the unlabeled path with three edges, and for n in N let g_{P_3}(n) := max{|F| : F is a family of simple graphs on the labelled vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n} such that for every G_1,G_2 in F, the edge-intersection G_1 ∩ G_2 contains a copy of P_3}. Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that g_{P_3}(n) <= (1-c)2^{binom(n,2)-1} for every n >= 4? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, can the trivial upper bound g_{P_3}(n) <= 2^{binom(n,2)-1} be improved by a multiplicative constant factor bounded away from 1 uniformly in n? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
justification: The paper first defines H-intersecting families and g_H(n) in Section 4, then discusses the P_3 case separately. It records that the older stronger conjecture g_{P_3}(n) = 2^{binom(n,2)-3} for all n >= 4 was disproved, and immediately replaces it with Conjecture 4.5, which is exactly the constant-factor improvement question appearing in your draft. So the right paper-faithful sharpening is not a broader characterization problem and not the disproved exact-value conjecture, but precisely the stand-alone P_3 formulation above with the definitions made explicit. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
